edges.reason: transfer forwards its arguments to transferFrom(msg.sender, _to, _value).
transferFrom invokes ensure(_from, _to, _value) before moving balances.
ensure calls condition(_from, _value) for non-whitelisted senders.
ensure compares _from/_to against the privileged owner address.
ensure whitelists the tradeAddress state variable.
ensure reads the UNI router constant when computing the pair.
ensure checks the canSale whitelist mapping for the sender.
condition reads _onSaleNum[_from] to enforce the per-address sale cap.
condition reads _minSale to bound the transfer value.
condition reads _maxSale to bound the transfer value.
condition reads _saleNum as the overall sale limit.
transferFrom does unchecked balanceOf[_from] -= _value and balanceOf[_to] += _value, allowing overflow/underflow without SafeMath.
transferFrom reads and decrements allowance[_from][msg.sender].
transferFrom increments _onSaleNum[_from] after the transfer.
delegate() feeds attacker-controlled calldata into the low-level delegatecall operation.
delegate() gates execution on msg.sender == owner.
init writes the _minSale state variable.
init writes the _maxSale state variable.
init writes the _saleNum state variable.
batchSend mutates balanceOf with unchecked += and -= and total = _value * _tos.length, enabling overflow.
setTradeAddress writes the tradeAddress whitelist state variable.
approve writes allowance[msg.sender][_spender] = _value.
approve uses msg.sender as the allowance owner.
transferFrom uses msg.sender as the spender for allowance checks.
transfer passes msg.sender as the _from address to transferFrom.
constructor assigns owner = msg.sender.
constructor mints the whole supply to balanceOf[msg.sender].
constructor sets totalSupply = _supply * 10**decimals.
constructor grants infinite allowance to the UNI router.
msg.sender must equal owner to pass the require guard in delegate().
init requires msg.sender == owner before setting sale parameters.
batchSend requires msg.sender == owner before mass transfers.
setTradeAddress requires msg.sender == owner before whitelisting an address.
constructor derives the owner role directly from msg.sender.
The delegatecall executes code from an external address inside the caller's context, a re-entrant execution path back into delegate().
SafeERC20 low-level call into a token contract can re-enter transferFrom during token transfer flow.
